title: List edge-colouring with no extra colours
decision_reason: Precise primary formulation, independently authored scholarly corroboration, full relevant claim-scope comparisons, duplicate audit and separated A45 self-review passed.
aliases: equality of list and ordinary chromatic indices

problem_fingerprint.objects: Every finite loopless multigraph G=(V,E) with at least one edge; parallel edges are allowed and count as distinct adjacent edges.
problem_fingerprint.model: Each edge e has an arbitrary finite list L(e) of permissible colour labels. Distinct edges sharing an endpoint must receive different labels.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every such G and every list assignment satisfying |L(e)| >= chi'(G) on all edges, there exists a proper edge colouring c with c(e) in L(e).
problem_fingerprint.observable: The list chromatic index chi'_ell(G), the smallest list-size guarantee that works for every assignment.
problem_fingerprint.conclusion: Prove or disprove chi'_ell(G)=chi'(G), where chi'(G) is the ordinary chromatic index.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Offline existence for all loopless multigraphs, with no algorithmic running-time condition. One canonical problem, including its simple-graph and complete-graph special cases. Neither vertex list colouring nor online paintability, correspondence colouring, edge recolouring, or a Delta+1 bound is the target.

source_records.title: Signed list edge coloring in graphs of bounded treewidth
source_records.version: Exact arXiv v1, August 20, 2026; cited as preprint, not as a read journal version.

resolution_comparisons.result: Equality for K_(p+1), p an odd prime, also in the painting game.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Only a complete-graph family, not arbitrary multigraphs.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorems 1.1–1.2 address K_(p-1) and K_(2p), p odd prime. Corollaries 6.3–6.4 delete specified cross-matchings or one perfect matching; the K_(p-1) deletion needs p>=5.
resolution_comparisons.difference: No theorem covers all multigraphs. Proposition 6.1's general even-order deletion consequence assumes a nonzero signed count; it does not establish that assumption for every order.

resolution_comparisons.result: Fractional and list indices agree up to a relative error tending to zero; expected-polynomial algorithms achieve asymptotic list sizes.
resolution_comparisons.difference: The degree threshold depends on the error parameter. Shrinking the error to force exact integer equality for a fixed graph is unjustified.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorem 5 assumes simple graphs, sufficiently large maximum degree Delta, minimum degree at least ln^25 Delta, and lists at least (1+epsilon) times the larger endpoint degree.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Both the degree condition and the extra list-size allowance remain. Theorem 8 likewise uses a strict interior matching-polytope condition.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorem 1.4 bounds the size of the intersection of all incident edge lists at each vertex, with local degree/multiplicity conditions; its third case is bipartite.
resolution_comparisons.difference: List cardinality alone gives no common-intersection bound. In particular incident edges can have disjoint lists. Full algorithmic clause is conditional on polynomially bounded intersection input.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorem A.1 requires list size at least Delta+q, where q=10^24 ln(n)+10^4(Delta^(3/4) ln(Delta)^(1/2)+Delta^(2/3) ln(n)^(1/3)).
resolution_comparisons.difference: This is an online algorithm with explicit additive slack and a known-degree assumption, not exact offline list-index equality.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorem 7 and Lemma 8 concern Kempe equivalence of ordinary edge colourings.
resolution_comparisons.difference: A Kempe swap need not preserve arbitrary lists; the claims therefore do not establish the target.

resolution_comparisons.result: Theorem 1 uses lists of size (3/2+epsilon)Delta, large Delta outside the bipartite case, and bounds communication rounds.
resolution_comparisons.difference: Communication efficiency under a larger list budget does not supply the exact chi'(G)-sized guarantee.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Signed list edge-colouring for two bounded-treewidth classes; at most maximum degree plus one colours.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Even the all-negative-sign ordinary specialization remains a restricted simple-graph class and does not ensure exactly the ordinary chromatic index for arbitrary loopless multigraphs.
